direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Pinned title over portraits
hero.blueprint: A pale flat ground. The title runs on one line of extra-bold uppercase at clamp(90px, 10vw, 160px), centred, spanning about 82% of the width, its cap line 120px from the top. It lives in a sticky layer (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh`) stacked above the images and set in one saturated ink that reads on both ground and photograph. Beneath it a single portrait photograph, 2:3, sits centred on columns 5–8 (about 37% of the width) and runs from 90px below the top edge down to the bottom edge, so the title crosses its upper quarter and the middle letters sit on the image. The wordmark sits top-left at 24px in 15px bold; one 'Menu' word sits top-right. Bottom-left on columns 1–3: the supporting sentence as a narrow column at 16px bold, max 26ch, its last line 32px above the bottom edge. Bottom-right: the single action as a solid rectangular button. As the page scrolls, further portraits of identical ratio and position replace the first, five to eight in all, each bringing its own flat ground colour sampled from the photograph, before the layer releases.
hero.mobile: The title stays pinned at the top at 17vw on one line, or two lines at 15vw if longer than ten characters. Each portrait becomes full width minus 16px margins at 2:3 and starts behind the lower half of the title. The supporting sentence follows the first portrait at 16px. The action button is fixed to the bottom-right corner, 16px in. The wordmark shrinks to a monogram top-left.
hero.headline: The title of the series, or the name: one uppercase line of up to about 14 characters at 10vw, two short lines on a phone.

palette.note: Deep red text on grey paper holds most of the page, then pale grey text on a solid red field takes one long section and the footer. Photographs are desaturated so nothing breaks the pair, and the button is a solid red block.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Keep the pinned run under six screens. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Full-bleed sequence, text interlocked
sections.blueprint: Three photographs, each 100vw by 100svh, shown one after another with nothing between them. Each is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside a wrapper 300svh tall, so the second slides up over the first and the third over the second like a curtain; no scroll hijacking. The section above interlocks with the first photograph: a narrow paragraph at 13–14px, 220px wide, sitting on the column line at 58% of the width, is pulled down with a negative bottom margin so its last four lines overlap the photograph's top edge, in a colour that reads on both ground and image. Each photograph carries one caption line at 15px in white at the bottom-left margin, over a neutral dark scrim limited to the lowest 120px. No heading. Choose three frames with the same light and a calm lower-left corner. The last photograph releases into the next section.
sections.mobile: Each photograph is 100vw by 88svh in a portrait crop and still sticks so the next covers it. The interlocking paragraph sits at the left margin, 60% wide, overlapping the first photograph by three lines. Captions stay bottom-left at 14px.

sections.name: Pinned heading, passing rows
sections.blueprint: One flat saturated field, full-bleed, as tall as its content. Columns 1–5: the heading, two or three words, at clamp(56px, 6.6vw, 104px) in the heaviest weight, position: sticky; top: 32px, so it holds while the right side travels. Columns 7–12: four to six capability blocks stacked with 120px between them. Each block is a title at 28px bold, then a two-part row: a portrait photograph at 3:4, 180–220px wide with square corners, and beside it, top-aligned, a plain list of four to six short lines at 18px with 14px between lines. Photographs alternate between the left and the right of their list, so the column does not read as a ladder. One ink colour, chosen for contrast on the field. The heading releases when the bottom of the last block reaches it.
sections.mobile: The heading becomes a sticky bar at the top of the section: one line at 9vw on the field colour with 12px padding, holding while blocks pass under it. Each block stacks its title, a full-width 4:3 photograph, then the list at 17px. 72px between blocks.

sections.name: Pinned sentence, photographs pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300svh tall. Inside it a `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds one sentence of 8–14 words, centred, three lines at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 68px), leading 1.1, in a block 62% of the viewport wide. The sentence is a paragraph, not a heading; it is white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` (or a solid ink that reads over every photograph) and has a higher `z-index` than the images. Behind it, three photographs sit in normal flow at different sizes and sides and scroll past the fixed sentence: a 4:5 portrait 24vw wide with its left edge at 6vw; 70svh lower a 16:10 landscape 38vw wide touching the right margin; 70svh lower a 1:1 frame 18vw wide starting at 30vw. Each crosses the sentence once. When the wrapper ends, the sentence releases and scrolls away with the last photograph. No scroll hijacking.
sections.mobile: Wrapper 260svh. The sentence pins at 40% of the screen height at 8.4vw, four or five lines, with 20px margins. Photographs alternate: 64% wide on the left margin, 78% wide on the right margin, then 52% on the left, with 50svh between them.

sections.name: Quotes in the gutters
sections.blueprint: A sticky stage (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh`) inside a wrapper three or four viewports tall. The section's title, two or three words at 10–12vw, stays pinned across the top of the stage. In the centre a portrait photograph, 4:5 and about 30vw wide, changes at each scroll step. Each step also brings one quotation, placed in an outer gutter in a column 280px wide and at a different height each time: right gutter in the upper third, then left gutter at mid-height, then right gutter in the lower third. Quotations are bold at 22px with tight leading; the speaker's name follows at 15px in the softer ink. Only one quotation shows at a time. Each step may switch the stage to its own flat ground colour. Drive the steps with an IntersectionObserver on spacer blocks; never hijack the scroll.
sections.mobile: No pinning. The title sits once at 16vw. Each speaker then gets a block: the portrait at 72% width, flush left and flush right in turn, the quotation at 20px beneath it on the same edge, and the name under that. Leave 72px between blocks.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Glitch&Grit
references.idea: Every screen is one project: two half-width footage columns with the project name stacked dead centre across their seam in a single flat pastel that changes per project.
references.hero: Black viewport split down its vertical centre. The left half holds a huge flat grey flower silhouette bleeding off the left and bottom edges; the right half is black with a few tiny video thumbnails drifting through. Dead centre, straddling the split, sits a two-line uppercase title in mint green, about 11vw per line, lines almost touching, spanning roughly 70% of the width. Two tiny category lines sit directly above it and a tiny 'view full project' link directly below, all in the same green. Navigation is six small bold white words pinned to the frame: three links across the top edge, the three-part studio name across the bottom edge.
references.type: Elza only, weight 900, uppercase, tracking -0.05em so letters nearly collide, line-height under 1. Just two sizes exist: roughly 158px project titles and 12px bold caps for nav, tags and links, a 13:1 jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #000000 #999999 #9ae187 #93f1f7 #dcc8ff #fbb060 — Black ground and dark-graded footage. The only flat colour is the title lock-up, which takes a new candy pastel per project: mint, cyan, lilac, cornflower, lemon, orange.
references.imagery: Client film footage in two half-width columns per screen, cropped tight, graded dark, square edges, the two columns vertically offset against each other. One flat grey cut-out flower shape opens the sequence.
references.layout: No margins or containers. Each project is a full viewport cut into two equal media columns with one centred title lock-up. Fixed corner navigation frames every screen; fourteen screens repeat the same slide with different footage and title colour.

sections.description: Each scroll stop is a project slide. Two half-width media columns fill the viewport edge to edge and travel vertically at different offsets, so their top and bottom seams never align. Centred over the join: a two-line 11vw uppercase title in one flat pastel, with two or three 12px tag lines stacked above and a 12px 'view full project' or 'coming soon' line beneath. Title colour changes on every slide; nothing else does.

There is no footer block. The last screen is simply another project slide, and the studio name fixed along the bottom edge in three pieces (first word bottom-left, ampersand bottom-centre, last word bottom-right) does the footer's job on every screen, mirroring the three nav words fixed along the top edge at the same size and weight.

steal: Break the studio name into three words pinned bottom-left, bottom-centre and bottom-right, mirroring three nav links across the top, so the viewport frame itself is the logo.
Give each project slide one flat pastel used only for its title and tags, so a colour change is the sole signal that the project changed.
Split the viewport into two media columns that scroll at different offsets and set the title across the seam so the type stitches the halves together.

references.name: NORMAL IS BORING
references.idea: The brand name is split and half of it turned upside down: a plain sans first word top-left and a serif last word flipped 180 degrees bottom-right stay fixed while panels slide sideways between them.
references.hero: A white panel fills the left 80%; a full-height interior photo takes the right 20%. Top-left: the first word of the name in light geometric capitals, about 56px. Bottom-right of the white panel: an italic 'is' above the last word in bold didone, rotated 180 degrees so it reads upside down. Three small caps nav links run vertically up the panel's right edge. The 50px headline is broken into three two-line fragments on different columns and baselines: one at 21% from the left, one a line lower at 42%, one back at 21% whose last word turns bold italic didone. A seven-line 13px paragraph hangs beneath the middle fragment.
references.type: Izmir, a light geometric sans in capitals, for wordmark, hero fragments and 13px body; Juana, a high-contrast didone, bold italic for accent words and huge roman capitals (10-12vw and larger, cropped) for scrolling statements; Editorial New ultralight for the reversed paragraph.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #ece4da #c7d7e9 #db5c59 #1f9aa0 — White and black panels alternate with warm beige; pale blue and coral panels appear deeper in. Type stays black or white. A single teal dot acts as cursor; photos bring wood and plant tones.
references.imagery: Warm interior and garden photography of finished homes in natural light, wood and linen tones. Square-cornered; used as full-height strips, full-bleed panels and smaller insets laid over larger photos by about a third.
references.layout: Reads as a sideways journey: white, black and beige panels slide horizontally with photos and oversized words cropped by panel edges. Text fragments sit on an irregular grid; the two halves of the logo stay fixed in opposite corners.

sections.description: The photo strip from the hero grows to a full-height panel while a second, smaller interior photo slides over it, overlapping by roughly a third. To the right a white panel carries a four-line statement in didone capitals about 90px tall, set so the lines run off the panel edge and are completed only as scrolling continues. A small 12px paragraph sits under the statement's left edge.

Full black panel. A nine-line paragraph in an ultralight serif at about 32px starts 70% of the way across and runs off the right edge; its words fade from white through grey to near-black line by line as a scroll-driven reveal. A single photo of a pool at dusk, roughly 300px square, sits alone in the lower-left third. The menu pill and flipped logo invert to white.

Values panel on beige. Along the left edge a vertical ticker repeats one word in 90px didone capitals rotated 90 degrees, separated by thin eight-point asterisks. Beside it a large exterior photograph of a stone-and-glass house with a bathroom photo about half its size laid over its lower-right corner, square edges, no shadow or border.

Beige panel where the project title is set so large that single didone letters exceed the viewport height and are cropped top and bottom, acting as black shapes in the left half. In the right half a modest 300px-wide aerial photo floats with a bracketed year above and a centred serif caption and two-line descriptor below.

steal: Split a two-part brand name into opposite corners of the viewport and flip one half 180 degrees so the logo enacts the name.
Break a headline into fragments on different columns and baselines, like a stair, and hang the body paragraph under one fragment only.
Scale a project title until single letters are taller than the viewport, then float a small captioned photo beside those cropped shapes.

references.name: Aardvark Book Club
references.idea: A book club dressed as a sweet shop: fat black type, tumbling 3D books and boxes on wavy colour fields, annotated with handwritten asides.
references.hero: A saturated yellow field with two large wavy blobs, pale yellow then orange, rising from the bottom. A three-line headline in Champ Bold, black, at about 8.3vw with leading under 0.85, is flush to a 15px left margin and reaches 60% across. Beneath it: a four-line paragraph 310px wide and a magenta split button (label plus arrow square). Right of centre a 3D hardback in navy and pink tilts 20 degrees, 600px tall; another book is cropped by the top-left corner, a third by the bottom edge. A purple handwritten note sits rotated at far right. Nav: pale-yellow pill links centred, an orange login button, black round social icons.
references.type: Champ Bold, an ultra-heavy wide sans with a looped g, for headings at 120px with tight tracking and leading; Degular for 18px body and pill labels; a purple handwritten script (Hello Organichand) for rotated margin notes and step labels. Three distinct voices.
references.colour: #ffd249 #faed8f #f9a21f #ffdbfd #a4f6f8 #fd48f2 — Each section owns one flat candy colour: yellow hero, white shelf, pink steps, cyan unboxing, deep violet footer. Type stays black; buttons are magenta.
references.imagery: 3D-rendered hardbacks and a patterned shipping box, cut out and tilted, floating over flat wavy vector shapes; real book covers on tilted coloured cards; black line drawings of figures on step cards. Nothing sits square to the grid.
references.layout: Sections are full-width panels with roughly 80px corner radius inset about 20px from the viewport, each a different colour. Headings alternate left and centre; cards overlap and rotate a few degrees; handwritten notes are tucked beside headings at an angle.

sections.description: White band. A centred black heading at 5.5vw over a two-line subline, with a rotated handwritten note at its upper left. Below, a horizontal row of book covers, each on a rounded colour-matched card with a small tag pill at top-left; cards tilt alternately by 3 degrees at staggered heights, the last cropped by the right edge, with two round arrow buttons above at right. Later, covers give way to same-coloured info cards with genre pills, heavy title and blurb.

A pale-pink rounded panel with lighter wavy shapes inside. Heavy black heading at left with a handwritten aside beside it; a small round logo stamp and a magenta split button at right. Along the bottom, four portrait cards about 250px wide in cyan, magenta, yellow and violet overlap like a fanned hand, each rotated a few degrees, with a handwritten step label at top, a black line drawing in the middle and a heavy caption at the foot.

A full-viewport cyan rounded panel containing only a 3D shipping box wrapped in a wavy magenta, violet and black pattern, centred. Across the scroll it goes from closed and tilted to lid open, growing to about 57% of the viewport width, with a single handwritten note at its right. No heading and no button.

The preceding white section ends in large rounded bottom corners over a deep violet footer. Left: white logo, two store badges, two magenta round social icons. Centre: the patterned box again, cropped by the bottom edge. Right: a small heavy heading, a white rounded email field and a magenta split button. A black legal strip closes the page.

steal: Give each section one flat saturated colour inside a large-radius inset panel and keep the type black across all of them.
Add rotated handwritten margin notes beside headings to carry secondary facts in a second voice.
Fan step cards so they overlap and tilt instead of sitting in an even grid.
